 Beer recall hits 2 more Canadian products, bringing total to 31
 By 
 Rachel Morgan 
 Global News 
 Posted November 13, 2026 10:05 am 
 3 min read 
 View image in full screen 
 Two products from a Quebec-based microbrewery are hit under a nationwide recall affecting 31 beer products. 
 Nam Y. Huh/AP Photo

 A Quebec-based microbrewery and restaurant operator has issued a beer recall for two of its products just three days after more than two dozen alcoholic and non-alcoholic beer products were pulled off the shelves nationwide from other brands.
 Archibald Inc. issued the recall for its Nuit Blanche White IPA 473 ml cans as well as four packs.
 A notification from the Canadian Food Inspection Agency says the product was recalled due to pieces of metal.
 The agency is requesting that all retailers cease the selling, serving or distributing of the affected products.
 The recall comes just days after Molson Canada 2005, the official Canadian subsidiary of Molson Coors Beverage Company, issued a recall for 29 of its products due to pieces of metal.
 Blue Moon, Black Horse, Brasseur de Montreal, Coors Light, Hop Valley, India Beer and Molson Canadian are the brands affected by the recall.

 The impacted Molson Canada, Coors Light, India and Black Horse products are sold in Atlantic Canada. Brasseurs de Montreal products are sold in Quebec and Hop Valley products are in Ontario and Western Canada. Select Blue Moon products are affected across all four regions.
 Story continues below advertisement 
 1:24 
 29 beer products recalled across Canada 
 In an email to Global News, Molson Coors said the impacted products are limited to specific case codes which vary by region.
 “Molson Coors Beverage Company is working closely with the Canadian Food Inspection Agency and our customers as we continue to investigate a quality issue affecting select products packaged at our Creemore, Longueuil, Moncton and St. John’s breweries,” the company said in a statement. “We have not received any notification of consumer harm to date.”
 The company added that defective products matching an impacted case code should be returned to its place of purchase.
 Molson Coors said the recall is Class III, meaning there is a “low risk that consuming the food may result in undesirable health problems.”
